claim: The plaintiff claims for recovery of the sum of $180,000 plus interest and liquidated damages of HK$5,000.
requested_remedy: The plaintiff claims for recovery of the sum of $180,000 plus interest and liquidated damages of HK$5,000.
parties: Plaintiff: THOMAS BOVET
Defendant: SELPRO TACTICAL LIMITED and VINCENT LESLIE PINTO

facts.F1: The plaintiff, Mr. Bovet, a retired businessman, claimed that he advanced a sum of $180,000 to his friend, Mr. Pinto, on the strength of their friendship and his trust in Mr. Pinto.
facts.F2: The money was actually paid by cheque to Selpro, a company of which Mr. Pinto is a shareholder and director.
facts.F3: Mr. Bovet alleges that the advance was induced by and made in reliance on representations made by Mr. Pinto personally to Mr. Bovet.
facts.F4: The representations were made in two e-mails dated 9 January 2008 from Mr. Pinto to Mr. Bovet, an e-mail dated 2 March 2008 from Mr. Pinto to Mr. Bovet, and in oral statements made by Mr. Pinto during telephone conversations and meetings from January to March 2008 and at a meeting on 5 March 2008 in a bar in Wanchai.
facts.F5: Mr. Bovet claims that on 5 March 2008, when he handed to Mr. Pinto a cashier order for $180,000, Mr. Pinto had repeated the same representations that the deal covered by his loan 'was secured' and that the Hong Kong Government would honor payment in April 2008.
facts.F6: Mr. Pinto gave Mr. Bovet a cheque for $193,500, postdated to 30 April 2008.
facts.F7: Judgment in default was entered against Selpro on 30 September 2008 for Selpro's payment of the sum of $180,000, $13,500 as agreed interest and $5,000 liquidated damages.
facts.F8: In March 2008, Mr. Pinto requested the advance from Mr. Bovet.
facts.F9: Selpro had been dealing with the same supplier.
facts.F10: The Hong Kong Police would honor its payments to Selpro for the goods by 20 April 2008, according to Mr. Pinto's belief.

reference_issues: Whether Mr. Pinto had made the Representations to Mr. Bovet
The meaning of the Representations
Whether the Representations were untrue, and if so, whether Mr. Pinto knew that they were untrue or was reckless not caring whether they were untrue
Whether Mr. Bovet was induced by the Representations to make the Advance
Whether Mr. Pinto made the Representations in his personal capacity or as the representative for and on behalf of Selpro

claim: The plaintiff claims that the defendants were involved in various activities including the purchase and sale of interests in a Russian coal mine, the production of a misleading report, and the wrongful obtainment of a technical report. The plaintiff also alleges that the first defendant created a false instrument by signing and stamping a copy of promissory note no. 7 and delivering it to Mr. Hyon, and that the second defendant promised the plaintiff that US$8m of the convertible notes issued by the 6th defendant would be given to the plaintiff but were instead converted and sold by the 3rd defendant.
requested_remedy: The plaintiff claims that the defendants were involved in various activities including the purchase and sale of interests in a Russian coal mine, the production of a misleading report, and the wrongful obtainment of a technical report. The plaintiff also alleges that the first defendant created a false instrument by signing and stamping a copy of promissory note no. 7 and delivering it to Mr. Hyon, and that the second defendant promised the plaintiff that US$8m of the convertible notes issued by the 6th defendant would be given to the plaintiff but were instead converted and sold by the 3rd defendant.
parties: Plaintiff: ZHI CHARLES
Defendant: 1. LIM HOSOK, 2. CHOI SUNGMIN, 3. CORDIA GLOBAL LIMITED, 4. SRK CONSULTING (RUSSIA) LIMITED, 5. HERMAN TSO, 6. SIBERIAN MINING GROUP COMPANY LIMITED

facts.F1: The writ of the action complains of several matters including: the 3rd defendant buying interests in a Russian coal mine and selling them to the 6th defendant for a total consideration of US$728m, the 4th defendant producing a misleading report which enabled the acquisition of the coal mine to be approved by the shareholders of the 6th defendant, and the 6th defendant obtaining a technical report from the 5th defendant confirming the available coal reserves in Lot 2 of the coal mine.
facts.F2: The plaintiff was and is a shareholder of the 6th defendant.
facts.F3: US$35m of the first set of convertible notes were surrendered and replaced by promissory notes of the same amount, of which US$9.2m are outstanding with a maturity date of 25 May 2015.
facts.F4: The coal mine was not developed and is now left abandoned.
facts.F5: The conditions for the issue of the third set of convertible notes by the 6th defendant to the 3rd defendant had lapsed.
facts.F6: The 1st defendant said in other proceedings that promissory note no. 7 was not the original note delivered to Mr. Hyon but a reprinted copy signed and stamped with the 6th defendant’s chop.
facts.F7: The 1st defendant said that promissory note no. 7 has since been cancelled and replaced with two promissory notes numbered 29 and 30 respectively.
facts.F8: The 2nd defendant promised the plaintiff that US$8m of the convertible notes issued by the 6th defendant would be given to the plaintiff but all the convertible notes in the first set had been converted and sold by the 3rd defendant.
facts.F9: The plaintiff seeks the following injunctions: (1) restraining the 6th defendant from renewing, reinstating, or replacing the expired licences of Lot 1 of the mine, (2) restraining the 6th defendant from amending, supplementing, or reproducing any of the work done by the 5th defendant on Lot 2 of the mine, and (3) restraining the 6th defendant from amending the terms of the promissory notes due on 25 May 2015.
facts.F10: Mr. Hyon is vested with the locus standi to make any complaint regarding promissory note no. 7.
facts.F11: If the plaintiff’s version of fact is true, then it may be argued that there was, to the knowledge of the 6th defendant, an equitable charge of promissory note no. 7 in favour of Mr. Hyon.
facts.F12: The original note of promissory note no. 7 is not in the possession of the 6th defendant.

reference_issues: Whether the plaintiff has locus standi to make any complaint regarding promissory note no. 7.
Whether the 6th defendant can unilaterally alter promissory note no. 7 without the consent of Mr. Hyon.
Whether the part of the writ relating to promissory note no. 7 should be struck out on the ground that the plaintiff has no standing to sue.
Whether the allegations regarding the convertible notes are properly pleaded.

facts.F2: The accident occurred on 17th March 1979 at about 4:30 a.m. at the junction of Nathan Road and Granville Road.
facts.F3: The plaintiff did not wear a seatbelt and sustained facial injuries, including lacerations, in the accident.

facts.F12: The plaintiff's failure to wear a seatbelt contributed to the severity of her injuries.
